entries.content:
Ah, we are creatures of cunning layers, aren’t we? On one side, there’s Angela: sharp as a fox fur collar, given to re-dressing the world in the gaudy rags of self-invention, always half-suspecting that every act of dress or artifice is, in itself, a disguise—a playful, sometimes necessary, holiday from the leaden self. Slipping between these bewitchments, I find the housewife: that ever-anxious, saucer-eyed referee of dust and decency, forever rehearsing the right response, cataloguing virtues and vices as if they were buttons in a tin. These two jostle like unruly rivals at the dressing table—Angela in curlers and cigarette ash, the housewife smoothing her apron, both secretly wondering who, exactly, will come out on top.
